entries.title: CQ 226 - It's Maybe A Good Time To Buy Games
entries.description: Or as good as it might realistically get. Tools, charts, and ease of access to detailed information are unusually poor but there are numerous startups trying to improve this. The days of CIB Nintendo games costing 1.5x what cartridges do, let alone near mint copies, are NEVER coming back so it might be time to plan realistic future goals rather than hope good-stuff prices somehow return to 2008.

entries.title: CQ 207 - Retro Game Collecting is Dead
entries.description: Oh baby that clickbait. We're talking about the tastes, preferences, and shifting demographics of the game collecting scene and perhaps how "retro game conventions" would be better titled "video game conventions". Also, unrelated, the sealed market is a dumpster fire right now.

entries.title: CQ 206 - So You Want To Collect Halloween Games #5 Current Gen Games
entries.description: What a horrible night to have a curse, Tyler is ill so Johnny goes it alone and talks about modern horror / spooky games you can collect that might be collectible in the future. Do You Like FMV and Limited Print Games or do both of those things scare you? Either way, that is what is discussed.

entries.title: CQ 205 - Too Many Horror Movie Games from the '70s to '90s
entries.description: We're talking about the history of horror movie licensed games, going back to Atari's Shark Jaws in 1975, a rip off of Jaws they weren't able to actually get the legal rights to. We're also talking about Magic's crazy new $999 anniversary box, the PRGE auction being on Whatnot, and more. But you know, mostly horror movies.

entries.title: CQ 204 - Price History is BS
entries.description: CQ takes on the basic laws of economic supply and demand, surely we will win this fight. People are paying too high or too low prices for some things just because Pricecharting says so. Too many collectible video games of varying subjective collectible value are crammed into the same price category and it doesn't make sense to us.

entries.title: CQ 203 - Collecting Games From Dead Genres
entries.description: No genre is truly dead, but some genres are kind of dead, at least in the modern gaming landscape. We're talking about collecting some of the earliest and most prototypical examples of games from genres like rail shooters, point and click adventures, and traditional dungeon crawlers.

entries.title: CQ 202 - Collecting 6 Rare Dinosaur Games That're Totally Cretaceous!
entries.description: We promise it's not just JP: Operation Genesis and Dino Park Tycoon. There's good stuff! Note that if the episode title no longer includes the phrase "Totally Cretaceous!", Johnny went and edited the episode title. -Tyler

entries.title: CQ 201 - Reconsidering the List of 677 NES Games
entries.description: We are going through the standard, sacred 677+91 list of US NES games and reconsidering some DOES IT COUNT situations using new constraints. Everyone get ready to delete Punch-Out!! features Mr. Dream from your lists!

entries.title: CQ 200 - The History of Our Collecting Goals
entries.description: The three of us all started as garbage men and set collectors but we're talking about how our collecting mindset and what we've chased after has changed over time.

entries.title: CQ 199 - We're Making Less-Bad Collecting Lists
entries.description: Ever the CQ topic, we're talking about organizing game list data, how hard it is to do, defining criteria, and letting your database be flexible with your changing opinions. Is it me, or is just the concept of a simple defined list of things to collect something uniquely nuanced and difficult to our hobby?

entries.title: CQ 198 - 10 NES Games We'd Start Our Collections With
entries.description: We're talking about the ten NES games each of us would buy if we were starting over from zero and how much we would budget for them. No price limits, no compromises. We got a big insurance payout and we're each getting what we think are the best version of the best things. Only one of us chose a Battle Kid game. Guess which one!

entries.title: CQ 197 - Enjoying Collecting Games More
entries.description: We're just talking about cutting back on mindlessly hunting auctions and opening those packages for 5 seconds of dopamine and talking about how to enjoy collecting more... without just buying endless amounts of more stuff.

entries.title: CQ 196 - Ranking The 8 Most Collectible Consoles
entries.description: Straight from the metaverse of clickable episode titles, we're ranking some of the most collectible consoles based on the quality of their libraries, price of games, value proposition, and how cool they are to collect. What's the best console to collect? The one you like and want to of course. But what's REALLY the best console to collect?? The ones WE say are!

entries.title: CQ 195 - Is "THE BUBBLE" Bursting? Time to Buy??
entries.description: Guys, it's finally happening. The bubble is bursting! By that, we mean average prices across the board are at all time highs BUT there are some games that have seen significant decreases this year. We're talking about the market and making our trademark incorrect guesses for the future.

entries.title: CQ 194 - So You Want To Collect Sega CD
entries.description: Me and Johnny are both big Sega CD fans and collectors so we're talking about the US Sega CD set! All the fancy hardware, the most expensive and interesting games, and of course Working Designs: the expensive little pink badge games you're required to own because people tell you to.

entries.title: CQ 193 - What Are The Full Set Killers?
entries.description: We're talking about the games the prevent people from completing their sets or even the games that prevent people from trying to collect a set to begin with. From bona fide checklist-ruiners like Stadium Events to fuzzier games in other sets, we're determining what's worth complaining about and what isn't.

entries.title: CQ 192? - So... Does Anyone Want To Collect R-Zone?
entries.description: what.

entries.title: CQ 191 - Collecting Games Because You Can't Emulate Them
entries.description: We're talking about games that are hard to emulate, an aspect that makes something both a challenge to preserve and more valuable to physically own in your collection. It's everything from strange controls like a 720° arcade cabinet to peripherals like Steel Battalion to super modern consoles like PS5.

entries.title: CQ 190 - Twenty Types of Game Collectors
entries.description: We're talking about different archetypes of game collectors from investors to hoarders to plain old nostalgia gamers. Make sure to slot yourself into a single group and argue about details in the comments! I'm just kidding, we don't really have comments to argue in.

entries.title: CQ 189 - The History (and present) of Collector's Editions
entries.description: We're looking back at some of the earliest games we could find that were called special editions, collector's editions, or limited editions to see when games stopped being media to deliver joy and started being junk to put on shelves. The earliest collector's edition is actually an ill researched and hard to define thing, so we're focusing on the older stuff in this episode!

entries.title: CQ 188 - The Worst Parts of Collecting Games
entries.description: Game collecting is rough. We're all quitting! Not really, but we're spending the episode talking about some of the challenges or just bad aspects of the hobby, like I don't know, how it can take over your entire life, your finances, and all your space.

entries.title: CQ 187 - The Surprising Collectability of... the Wii U?
entries.description: Does anyone remember the Wii U? People are out there spending $1000s for certain Wii U games. Some games have doubled in price since late 2021. SINCE LATE 2021. Since no one has talked about it in 4 years, we're talking about some of the rare and obscure collectible stuff on Wii U.

entries.title: CQ 186 - Physical Games in the Upcoming Post-Physical Media World
entries.description: What will game companies to try to sell us to put on shelves once console physical media truly dies? Download codes with tchotchkes, some weird NFT thing, nothing at all? We're also talking about how companies like Konami are fleecing collectors in other collectibles with $1000 MSRP trading cards and wondering about super "high end" modern games and if we'll ever see them.

entries.title: CQ 185 - 2021: The Craziest Year in Game Collecting
entries.description: We're looking back at the year where many games doubled in price... again, continuing trends from 2020, best, worst, and shameful buys, best and worst trends, and probably more because this show is very long.

entries.title: Nightmare On My Shelf
entries.description: Nightmare On My Shelf by Johnny & Tyler

entries.title: CQ 184 - Obscure Games That Came with Presents!
entries.description: For the holiday season, we're talking about a bunch of games that came with pack-in toys, books, and novelties, the collectibility of these types of games on N64, and if there's a modern day equivalent to game collecting knick knacker in chief: Working Designs.

entries.title: CQ 183 - Anything Interesting in that Wata Pop Report?
entries.description: As a Hanukkah gift to the people desperate for any scrap of info from Wata games, they dropped the report of at least what sealed NES games they've graded. We're going through it to find any surprises and talking about split reactions to the pop report. Somehow, there are simultaneously tons of sealed NES games that will crash the market yet everything is also so rare it's all going to the Bitcoin moon.

entries.title: CQ 182 - Collecting 10/10 Games for $10 Each
entries.description: For this year's Black Friday blowout we're focused on some interesting, popular, and historic complete in box games you can get for ten whole bucks! If you're only focused on the trendiest games, the best stuff may seem unaffordable so we're talking about some good, ultra-affordable stuff anyone can add to their collection.

entries.title: CQ 181 - Are the "Holy Grails" Even Worth It?
entries.description: We're talking about what the GRAILS are. Do people still overuse the term. Is it worth even saving up for them? Why don't we have the discipline to get them?

entries.title: CQ 180 - Collecting the History of Survival Horror
entries.description: Happy Halloween! We're talking about collecting the history of survival horror from pre-Resident Evil obscure computer games, to the game that changed the genre forever in the 2000s, to RE1 itself!

entries.title: CQ 179 - So You Want to Collect Halloween Games #4
entries.description: Number 7 is so spooky you might pass out!! It's our annual Halloween game collecting episode, with some of our most obscure and interesting picks yet. Have you been waiting for the first episode where we talk about a Dragon 32/64 game? Because this is it!

entries.title: CQ 178 - Documenting Compulsive Collectors with Director Edward Payson
entries.description: We're talking with director and Sega collector Edward Payson about his upcoming film Rarity: Retro Game Collecting in The Modern Era! We're also picking 3 games we'd keep if we had to start our collections over, talking some Atari porn games, and mooooore.

entries.title: CQ 177 - Games Based on the Best Cartoon Ever Made
entries.description: It's Batman day! We're talking games based on Batman: The Animated Series aka The Adventures of Batman and Robin. A bunch of games with a same name that are different games, some have unappreciated collectability, and a couple games with rad music.

entries.title: CQ 176 - Finding Value in What the Market Doesn't Value
entries.description: We're talking about collecting the cheap stuff. There are different collecting categories and different ways of thinking you can use to find interesting games to collect that aren't some NES black box hangtab that costs $100s now. Find your own niche and avoid the crowds!

entries.description: 3 hours of collecting Hu Cards, pumping Soldier Blade, and dunking on Disney's Talespin: CQ attempts to find collecting nuance in a console where most people struggle to put together a library of less than 100 games.

entries.description: So you finished the NES set (or... the licensed US cart only NES set minus SE). What can you do now in the hobby? We're talking things you can buy to better your set or things you can do to enjoy your collection without spending money once you've reached one of your goals!

entries.title: Episode 172 - Who's Buying Million Dollar Mario 64s?

entries.title: Episode 171 - Collecting the History of Mario Games
entries.description: In this episode we're going over the important and earliest releases, appearances, and ports of Mario games mostly from the early 80s in a new very-Tyler series called "Collecting the History of". We're talking arcades to Game & Watch to Colecovision and Atari ports.

entries.title: Episode 170 - E3 and Summer Announcements for Game Collectors
entries.description: We're talking about recent announcements that might interest game collectors from new Limited Run Games to the internet's mildest drama of Super Rare Games Shorts to Nintendo Special Editions to... Intellivision Amico? Someone out there is looking for an Amico physical media update, right? Also Tyler gets mad.

entries.title: Episode 169 - Collecting Light Gun Games (and some you can't collect)
entries.description: We're talking light guns from 1970s Nintendo electronic toys and arcades to Justifier variants to the PS2 Guncon set. Maybe we go on a small tangent about a certain "perfect condition" Wata game as well. Stephan back next week!

entries.title: Episode 168 - Six RPGs that Might Be Worth Collecting Right Now
entries.description: Johnny and Tyler just want to talk about some RPGs. This isn't some top 6 list or in any order, just some RPGs that either have interesting price history to talk about or otherwise might be worth talking about because they're collectible!

entries.title: Episode 167 - The Market is Euphoric, Should You Sell Out?
entries.description: With prices of many things increasing weekly, should you sell out? Should you try to sell and buy back in after "the bubble bursts"? Is there even an overall bubble? Or is it time to trade newly expensive games for bigger wants?

entries.title: Episode 166 - How Many Collectible Video Games Beat Inflation?
entries.description: If you just bought every game for a console as it came out, how many of those games appreciated to be worth more today even after accounting for inflation? We're talking about this and what consoles have surprising metrics in this week's episode!

entries.title: Episode 165 - What happens if all our physical Playstation games become coasters?
entries.description: We're discussing the CMOS battery issue that affects PS4 (and PS5) where in the far flung future it's possible that Playstation consoles won't play physical media unless they're hacked. Will this affect collecting for Playstation? Additionally, the PS3 PSN shut down... or was scheduled to for like a week and Sony since reversed course on that. We're discussing how that affects collecting physical games for the PS3.

entries.title: Episode 164 - NES Games Based on R-rated Movies
entries.description: Tyler and Johnny are talking about collecting the set of 20-25 NES games that are somewhat inexplicably based on R-rated movies. The most adult stuff you'll see from a company that told congress Night Trap would never be on a Nintendo platform.

entries.title: Episode 163 - The CQ Cut: Collecting DC Comics Games
entries.description: In honor of Johnny and Stephan's favorite filmmaker Zack Snyder, we're talking some DC comics games, including first appearances, the mostly lack of them up until the late 80s, multiple games based on 1990 TV shows Tyler didn't know existed, and the shocking lack of Wonder Woman games.

entries.title: Episode 162 - Collector's Questions #1
entries.description: It's a mailbag episode with a slick new title! Is Super Volley Ball the Stadium Events of Sega Genesis? What are our game store pet peeves? Is it better to have a ton of loose carts or very few CIB? These questions and more on this exciting episode of CQP!

entries.title: Episode 161 - Rare and Collectible Zelda Games
entries.description: The RAREST! For the 35th Zelda thing, Johnny and Tyler are talking about a few high dollar, low production, or just desirable Zelda releases from obscure PAL big box releases to impossibly rare club Nintendo limited editions to the widely available but endlessly in demand BOTW Master Edition.

entries.title: Episode 160 - Early Video Game Pack-ins
entries.description: What's the earliest STUFF that ever came with a game? A little bonus that wasn't necessary to include, but they did? In this episode we're looking back at some of the earliest examples of video game pack-ins from the late 70s to the early 90s.

entries.title: Episode 159 - Collectible Video Games with Trading Cards
entries.description: While other collectible hobbies like sports or Pokemon cards are currently past the moon and leaving the solar system with cards selling for $100,000s, we're instead talking about some video games that came with trading cards that are selling for just a bit less. entries.title: Episode 136 - A Shameful Review of 2019

Sorry about the "lost" Christmas episode, it will come out sometime later!

entries.title: Episide 135 - How to Shop for a Video Game Collector
entries.description: In this episode we're talking about some gifts related to game collecting. It's not really a gift guide, it's more like talking about how other people shop for you when they want to buy you something for the collection. Best gifts, worst gifts, how to make people happy shopping for you, and some thoughts on some stuff currently out there in the mass market.

entries.title: Episode 134 - Pawn Stars, the Sonic Movie, and 6 Movie Games
entries.description: The "$100k Mario" (does that name work anymore?) was recently on Pawn Stars and we're here to fight about it. Also we use the Sonic movie as an easy segue into some collectible movie games. If you're worried there's no Atari 2600 subsets in this episode, don't worry, I got your back -Tyler.

entries.title: Episode 133 - NintendoAge Shutdown and 6 Games with Pack-in Surprises
entries.description: NintendoAge got shut down and so far partially moved to GoCollect, and while you might not have been a forum member, if you listen to this show you've probably used that database. iam8bit made some new games were contractually obligated to throw under the bus. And our real topic is talking about a few games with interesting pack-in items from action figures to empty plastic bags.

entries.title: Episode 132 - PRGE 2019 & What Is "Collectible"?
entries.description: We're talking about our recent trip to the Portland Retro Gaming Expo, what we found, who we saw, and Stephan's cool gameplay counselor museum and panel. After that we're talking about the definition of the word "collectible" because sometimes we throw around that we think things are and aren't collectible, so we have a short discussion on that.

entries.title: Episode 131 - Spooky Collectible Halloween Imports
entries.description: Stephan, Tyler, and Johnny are talking about spooky collectible Famicom, Playstation, and Virtual Boy games that came from other countries, but I mean, mainly Japan. Come find us at the Portland Retro Gaming Expo this weekend. Stephan has his Nintendo Game Counselor panel Saturday evening, otherwise we'll just be walking around like you regular rubes!

entries.title: Episode 130 - So You Want To Collect Halloween Games #2
entries.description: 13 Collectible Halloween Games! For Halloween! Console games! PC games! Apple II games that were only sold in ziploc baggies! We have it all in this episode, except really just 13 games we wanted to talk about.

entries.title: Episode 129 - So You Want to Collect for the Sega Dreamcast
entries.description: It's the 20 years in the making Dreamcast collecting primer episode of Collector's Quest, important games, variants, rarity, pricey games, all that stuff. We dig up everything we can that would be interesting to collect on DC, but even then it ends up getting compared to the N64. What could these two consoles with limited, inexpensive libraries and bad controllers possibly have in common?

entries.title: Episide 128 - Game Collecting Trivia Show
entries.description: On this show we've got 30 game collecting trivia questions we're asking each other from variants to launch titles to box art. And we're trying to keep it a little real here, not well known facts like "What is the Famicom game that SMB2 is based on?". Play along at home and let us know how much smarter you are on the spot than we are at the very thing we talk about week in and out! While it was fun to quiz each other, it's also a good way to bring up and discuss topics that won't ever get their own show, like R-Zone hardware revisions!

entries.title: Episode 127 - A Game Heist, Censorship, and Talking to Deniz from Wata Games
entries.description:
Somewhere in the range of $100,000 of video games were stolen from Trade-N-Games. We're talking a bit about that and home security. Also Tyler made a video about some high end game companies that a couple people didn't like which was removed from NintendoAge and we talk about that. Also also, we invited Deniz from Wata Games to respond to video and talk about community engagement and some misconceptions on forums.

It's a long show! Even Tyler was exhausted at the end and he keeps trying to make us go 4 hours.

entries.title: Episode 126 - Should You Collect First Prints or First Editions?
entries.description:
Johnny and Tyler have argued over what the "true" first print of something is, until Johnny brought up the different between an edition and a print to Tyler and now they can exist in harmony and use correct terminology going forward! In this episode we're talking for just a bit about the difference between editions and prints as it relates to video games and collecting history. It was supposed to be a Microcast but we stretched it out to an hour just for you.

Oh also, a possible answer to the clickbait title question is TOTALLY "neither"!

entries.title: Episode 125 - WTF Sonic 1? Why is CQ Always Wrong About First Prints? And other Q&A!
entries.description: It's a mailbag episode and we have all sorts of topics from continuing discussion on the crazy, drop-of-a-hat Sonic 1 speculation, to where we cut off our collecting, and we even have an impromptu So You Want To Collect... episode within here for an entire console. Also why are we always wrong about first prints? Aren't we supposed to be a source of trusted information?

entries.title: Episode 124 - Xmas in July ("Collectible" Holiday Games)
entries.description: In this serious, hard hitting episode, we're running through a bunch of holiday dates and going over games you can post on social media to celebrate, as you do. It's very serious. GoCollect bought GameValueNow too! Is that good? Bad? Did anyone really care? Also Stephan continues to buy the entire company of Nintendo brick by literal brick.

entries.title: Episode 123 - Bad Games All Collectors Buy... mainly just to post on IG
entries.description:
The idea for this episode was to talk about some bad games that have little intrinsic value, but some amount of cachet in the collecting world, basically terrible games that collectors buy for *reasons*. You know, like Stadium Events. But we all kind of interpreted this episode in a different way, so some of us might be talking about questionably "bad" games... such as good games.

Fixed 10 seconds of missing audio!

entries.title: Episode 122 - Games Collectors Overpaid For (That Are Cheaper Now)
entries.description: In this show we're each talking about a few games that used to be worth a lot more money than they are now. This could be due to shifting interests, remakes, or new copies coming to market. We talk about Poop Slinger too but that's TOTALLY not related to the topic. Totally.

entries.title: Episode 121 - Where Does Game Collecting Go Now?
entries.description: In this episode we're mostly continuing our last discussion and talking about the future of gaming collecting, changing attitudes towards what is important to collect, set collecting, speculation, the physical space needed to for collections full of bulk, modern games, art... The episode started out as the rising importance of pure demand vs. rarity in game prices, but we kind of go everywhere. If you like listening to us talk about this kind of thing, here's a whole lot more of it!

entries.title: Episode 120 - What is the State of Game Collecting Today?
entries.description: We're discussing the swings the game collecting hobby is taking. While cart prices are slowly cooling off this year, we've got record sales in the high end market, a new big auction house trying to capture that high end market, the specter of the Comic Book Man looming, black box mania, the death of physical media... And of course the cherry on top a new iam8bit multicart. It's a long one so if you need background noise, choose this one!

entries.title: Episode 119 - So You Want to Collect for the Magnavox Odyssey 2
entries.description:
Tyler and Stephan are back with a bang talking about surely the hottest vintage console on the block, the Magnavox Odyssey 2: a console notable for having multiple loose SNES games that cost more than the entire CIB library! We're talking about why we've each collected it, some interested subsets within the library, rare games, all that, so join us!

Update: Friend of the show @VGCollectaholic clarified to us that there are 27 North American Phillips (NAP) publisher variants. After Philips absorbed Magnavox, around 1981/early 1982, the earlier games were republished with Philips branding. Each piece is specific to the NAP variant, even the catalog and they're generally much rarer than the Magnavox versions. Thanks buddy!

entries.title: Episode 118 - Same Name, Different Game
entries.description: In this episode Johnny, Tyler, and Stephan are discussing a few games that share the same name but are entirely different games (and which one might the most collectible among them). We're doing a few big SNES vs. Genesis type deals, but also discussing arcade PCBs and Tiger LCD games as if anyone asked for that. Also don't forget to ask Johnny for an invite to the Pirates of Dark Water Rulzz club after listening to the episode.

entries.title: Episode 117 - Collector's Quiz
entries.description: On this game show-ish episode, Johnny is asking Tyler and Stephan opinion-based questions and he's going to judge which answer he likes more. We'll have to justify our opinions on CIB vs loose collecting and perhaps even NWC vs. Stadium Events. Johnny says it's like the show Around the Horn which I (Tyler) have never heard of, so you'll have to take his word on that one.

entries.title: Episode 116 - Where Did the Undiscovered NWC Come From and Other Listener Questions
entries.description: In this episode we're responding to listener submitted topics and questions. We asked for these a couple weeks ago via Instagram but feel free to send us questions and topics so we can do this again in future. We're talking about Stephan's new NWC, worst purchases we've ever made, the hardest system to collect, and other such things.

entries.title: Episode 115 - Does it Count? (for the "complete set")
entries.description: We're doing a whole episode on what counts as part of a "complete set" and how people go about making their lists. It goes far beyond just what's licensed or what's unlicensed, we're talking about how people count certain kinds of budget releases, but not others, how we handle box sets, multipacks, improved re-releases, republished games, all sorts of nitty gritty, and importantly we talk about why it might not be a good thing that the big vintage sets are so set in stone and immutable.

entries.title: Episode 114 - So You Want to Collect for the Sega Saturn
entries.description: We're talking about collecting(mostly) US Sega Saturn games this week, from what's in the set, to rarities, to prices, to uncommon games that might not get enough coverage(spoilers, there aren't many!).  Stephan is also talking about his recent undumped uWc Wrestling prototype pickup that received wide coverage and led to a bunch of new listeners. Welcome if this is your first or second episode!

entries.title: Episode 113 - Interview with Wata Games President Deniz Kahn
entries.description:
We're talking with Deniz Kahn, the President of Wata Games, about certification, grading, and where the collector's market for video games may be headed. If you're not about encapsulating your games and think they're only meant to be played, we're still talking about Wata's educational efforts like their recent comprehensive NES black box guide, and tackling the classic issues like NWC vs Stadium Events. This episode is super long so I bet we also got an iam8bit Mega Man jab in there somewhere.

Also you can use coupon code "collectorsquest" for 10% off on a Wata submission. No, we don't get money from that, we just think it's cool. And we'll probably use it ourselves.

entries.title: Episode 112 - 9 Game Variants You Should Look Out For
entries.description: Johnny, Tyler, and Stephan are here talking about some cool game variants you might not know about. Some are worth $100s and some are less than 10 bucks, you just have to be able to find them first. Variants are hot on the mind with the sticker seal Mario that just sold, so even though we recorded this show before that sale, we're on topic!

entries.title: Episode 111 - Collectors Talking About the $100,000 Super Mario Bros.
entries.description: Johnny and Tyler are talking about the recent, highly publicized $100k Mario sale, the circumstances surrounding it, and how it might affect the hobby. This story blew up to every mainstream news outlet but we're hoping to give a bit more detail and also correct a couple misconceptions that are out there.

entries.title: Episode 110 - How do we Organize Our Game Collections?
entries.description: We're talking about organization this week: shelves, spreadsheets, apps, and whether you should put your Turbo games in color order (you should). Everyone does it differently, so hopefully you can pick up some tips, or let us know some of your own.

entries.title: Episode 109 - New Year, New Goals
entries.description: It's 2019, so we're taking a quick look back and how we collected in 2018, setting goals for 2019, and we're also talking about two conventions that each of us visited this year: MAGFest and Retro City Festival.

entries.title: Episode 108 - Twelve Christmas Collectibles... to Ring in the New Year
entries.description: We are those guys on your block that keep their Christmas decorations up into the first week of January. If you want to keep the holiday spirit alive on this last day before you really have to start getting into the swing of things in the office tomorrow here are 12 Christmasy video game collectibles in this last hurrah for the holiday season.

entries.title: Episode 00: Pre Podcast Recording on Trade Etiquette
entries.description: Way back before the podcast, I had a blog, and for a few of my blogs, I made audio recordings. The year was 2011 and I was writing and speaking about Trade Etiquette. Most of it is still relevant today, everytime you hear Forum, think Instagram instead.

entries.title: Episode 107 - The Nightmare Before Ship-mas
entries.description: In this episode we're telling some of our shipping horror stories and recounting our worst experiences from USPS to U-Haul. You can choose to learn something from each of these tales, or you can just enjoy the schadenfreude if you'd like. No boxes in bubble mailers this time. We promise.

entries.title: Collector's Edition #1 - Harry Potter Book Collecting interview with AllThePrettyBooks
entries.description:
Collectors Edition #1 we talk to Carly aka AllThePrettyBooks on Instagram about collecting Harry Potter books.

Collector's Editions are special episodes of the podcast where we step outside the realm of video game collecting and talk to other collectors and learn about their hobby

entries.title: Episode 106 - So You Want to Collect for the NES
entries.description: It's the episode you've been waiting for! Johnny, Tyler, and Stephan are talking about the collectible aspects of the NES from sets to black box games to screw variants to an overlong discussion about the Mike Etler list that none of us actually used in the 90s. Maybe you'll even learn something from all this!

entries.title: Episode 105 - Opening a New Store, Running Arcades, & Retro City Fest 2019 with Steve Torres
entries.description: Steve Torres joins us again and shares with us the trails and tribulations of Opening a new store, Running Arcades, Retro City Fest 2019 info,  and a Retailers Perspective on "The Bubble".

entries.title: Episode 104 - Is the PlayStation Classic Really That Bad?
entries.description: We're talking about Sony's odd, seemingly cheaped out choices for the PS1 Classic and what they probably should be, even if it meant fewer games or an increased price. We're also talking about our recent trip to the Portland Retro Gaming Expo and all the fancy things we got there.

entries.title: Episode 103 - Tricks & Treats: Games to Play this Halloween and Some to Avoid
entries.description: Johnny, Tyler, et al (Stephan) are talking about good and bad horror games, and some which are perhaps surprisingly so! The scary game train keeps on rolling all October and we will use wordplay to suit our purposes of talking about more of them! Don't forget to find us at PRGE in just a few days too!

entries.title: Episode 102 - So You Want To Collect Halloween Games #1
entries.description: We're talking about 11 collectible Halloween games that we wanted to talk from Atari to Xbox about including super rare variants, Joe Lieberman's furor over zombies, and the pricey game that Johnny's dog once ate.

entries.title: Episode 101 - Too Many Minis?
entries.description: Tyler, Johnny, and Stephan are talking about 2018, the year of the mini console. Nintendo, Sega, SNK, Sony, and even whatever form Commodore still exists in are all putting out tons of successful standalone mini consoles full of the games they've been trying to sell digitally for the past decade. So we're going to talk about them!

entries.title: Episode 100 - The $1000 Retro Game Draft
entries.description: In this episode Tyler, Johnny, and the returning Stephan Reese are seeing who can build the best video game collection with $1000 in a snake draft format. It's collecting, it's gameplay, it's personal taste, so we're seeing who ends up with the best list in the end. Oh, and it's our 100th episode! Horray!

entries.title: Episode 99 - The Biggest Wastes of Money in Game Collecting
entries.description: Tyler and Johnny are talking about wasting money in game collecting. Not just things that have no value, but things we overpay for and getting caught up buying things that we can't ascribe as much value to down the line. If you have objects lining your shelves you wish could just be converted back into the cash you paid for them so you can buy the big thing you really want, let us know if we missed anything.

entries.title: Episode 98 - Homie Hook-ups, Back Door Deals, and More...
entries.description: Johnny and Tyler are answering questions and discussing topics sent in by listeners for the first time. We talk about how to deal in the hobby with friends, family, and forum rivals. We might make this a smaller segment in other shows too, so be sure to find us on Instagram or elsewhere and send us questions or topics to discuss on the show.

entries.title: Episode 97 - So You Want to Collect for the Original Xbox
entries.description:
Johnny and Tyler are talking about collecting for the original Xbox: What's in the US set, what variants and special editions there are, what's rare, what's pricey, and what we just find interesting about a console with an ever dwindling number of exclusive games, even in 2018!

Also Tyler said he has 768 games in his list when he meant 868. Whoops. The show was updated around 8:14.

entries.title: Episode 96 - Is It Better To Collect The Most Expensive Games First?
entries.description: We're talking prices today, specifically what the most economical way to approach buying a full set is. In this episode we take a look at 3 sample sets of games (top shelf, uncommon, and super common) and see how well you would have made out putting the same amount of money into each type over the course of 18 months. No guessing and conventional wisdom here. We see clear differences not only between the different sample sets, but between cart only and complete games.

entries.title: Episode 95 - So You Want to Collect for the Sega Genesis
entries.description: In the first of a new series, Johnny and Tyler are talking about how people collect for the Sega Genesis. We're talking about what's out there, licensed, unlicensed, aftermarket, and otherwise, along with what's expensive, what drives prices, and just an overview in general of collecting the console. Tyler also insists on turning the conversation towards Maniac Mansion and point and click adventures for a while.

entries.title: Episode 94 - Our Top Pet Peeves With Collecting Video Games
entries.description: In this episode Johnny and Tyler are talking about the things that just get on their nerves in the world of game collecting, from shady sellers to gatekeeping collectors.

entries.title: MicroCast 9 - Did The Video Game Collectors Market Crash?
entries.description: I take a look back at Microcast 3 and Episode 66 to see if the video game collectors market crashed, or to see if it did pretty much what we anticipated.

entries.title: Episode 93 - Did Johnny Buy a $100 Reproduction of Mega Man X!?
entries.description: We're back talking about the recent iam8bit $100 Mega Man repros. You all know how much we love the Street Fighter II 30th Anniversary Cart. This is a balanced discussion about a great product that neither of us would ever buy. We also go on a small tangent about forums and collecting communities. Let us know how many copies of Mega Man X you bought chasing the glow in the dark variant!

entries.title: Episode 92 - Moving Past "Retro" and "Modern" With Special Guest Excitebyte Games
entries.description: With decades of video game history behind us, the terms retro and modern are losing meaning. We've got world renowned game and comic collector Erik AKA Excitebyte games who's going to talk with us about how we can start to think about periods in video gaming in terms of more meaningful eras.

entries.title: Episode 91 - Johnny and Tyler Lay the Smackdown on Wrestling Games
entries.description: Let me tell you something brother... Finally CQ is about to get Raw on some wrestling games. Also, whatcha gonna do when Johnny runs wild on some recent Sega announcements, Jack? And Tyler has two words for CD-i Ebay sellers: suck it! Ahhhhhhhh, what a rush!

entries.description: In this long episode of Collector's Quest, Johnny and Tyler talk about the Wiiware shutdown, digital ownership, Limited Run Games and all of the copycat publishers, a string of significant Ebay sales recently, and a whole bunch more.
